bio:
Elizabeth Sorber was the youngest named child of Abraham Sorber, a man "of German descent" who came from Northampton County to Hanover Township in Luzerne County about 1783 with a family of grown children, so she was probably born in Northampton County. Her brothers were John, who married Betsey Sleppy and moved to Butler Township, George (1778–1860), who married Elizabeth Ehra, Jacob, who married a Cease, and Henry, who also went to Butler Township.

Elizabeth married John Croop. The Croops came to Hunlock's Creek with "the numerous family of Sorbers", and the two families built the sawmills there; John Croop held 200 acres in what is now Hunlock Township and raised ten children. His son William Croop, born in Newport Township, married Mary Sorber of Northampton County, and their son Hiram Croop, born in 1832, is described as a grandson of both John Croop and Philip Sorber, a son of Jacob. If Elizabeth was William's mother, William married a Sorber cousin.
openQuestions: Was Elizabeth the mother of William Croop (b. Newport Twp., d. 1889 aged 84, per Bradsby)? Bradsby names William's father John Croop but not his mother.

GEDBAS 1435014144 (from an Ancestry tree) makes Abraham Sorber (b. 1744) a son of Jacob Sorber and Maria Engel Doll (H0459/H0215). That would make Elizabeth a granddaughter of Maria Engel. No primary record has been seen.

researchNotes: Plumb's History of Hanover Township (1885) lists Elizabeth as the youngest-named child of Abraham Sorber, 'of German descent', who came to Hanover from Northampton County about 1783 with grown-up children. Her siblings, as Plumb gives them: John (m. Betsey Sleppy; removed to Butler Twp.), George (b. 1778, d. 1860, m. Elizabeth Ehra), Jacob (m. ___ Cease) and Henry (removed to Butler Twp.). Plumb's entry for her is just 'Elizabeth Sorber, m. John Croop' ([R4-S1]). Bradsby (1893) says John Croop came to Hunlock's Creek with 'the numerous family of Sorbers' and that the two families built the sawmills there. In Bradsby, Hiram Croop (b. 1832) is a son of William Croop (born Newport Twp.) and Mary Sorber (born Northampton Co.), and William is a son of John Croop, who had 200 acres in what is now Hunlock Twp. and raised ten children. Bradsby does not name John's wife ([R4-S2]). If Elizabeth was William's mother, then William married a Sorber cousin. Munsell calls Hiram 'a grandson of both John Croop and Philip Sorber', and Bradsby makes Philip Sorber a son of Jacob.
summary: Daughter of Abraham Sorber of Hanover Township and wife of John Croop, of the families that settled Hunlock's Creek.
